turns.text:
be brutal. does this sound like im trying too hard

"hey lucas. so i was thinking about the drivetrain we put together in C7 on tuesday and honestly your gear ratio idea was pretty good i guess?? but i think mine handles torque better, wanna compare numbers thursday"

A little, yes. The "pretty good i guess??" reads like you're working hard to sound unbothered, and the double question mark adds to it. The competitive part is fine. It's the hedging that gives it away.

Tighter version:

"hey, been thinking about the drivetrain from Tuesday. I think my setup gets better torque than the gear ratio you proposed. Want to compare numbers at Thursday's meeting?"

It's short, specific and a bit challenging, with no padding. Want it even more casual?
ok yeah thats better. lol and to be clear hes my rival. i do have a crush on him but that doesnt change that, so it cant sound flirty AT ALL

Got it, so the goal is purely about the robot. The version above already avoids anything flirty: no compliments, no emoji, no "haha." Two more tweaks keep it strictly business:

"hey, thinking about Tuesday's drivetrain. I think my setup gets better torque than your gear ratio. Want to compare numbers Thursday in C7?"

I cut "been" and "at Thursday's meeting" so it sounds like a quick work note. If you want a bit more edge, swap the last line for "Bring your numbers."
bring your numbers is good. also unrelated, the kid i tutor said hes just dumb at math again. what do i say that isnt cheesy

Skip the "you're not dumb!" cheerleading. Kids tend to hear that as a script. Try something specific and calm:

"Dumb people don't finish that whole page. You just did. Math is a skill, so it gets better with practice, like anything else."

Or, if he's frustrated in the moment:

"That one is tricky. Let's look at where it got confusing. I bet it's only one step."

The second one works well because it turns a vague feeling ("I'm dumb") into a concrete problem he can fix. Praise the effort or the specific thing he got right rather than his ability in general. How old is he? I can tweak the tone.
seventh grade. second one is good. ok bye

Seventh graders usually respond well to that second one, especially if you sit next to him instead of across from him. Good luck Thursday. Final text:

"hey, thinking about Tuesday's drivetrain. I think my setup gets better torque than your gear ratio. Want to compare numbers Thursday in C7? Bring your numbers."
